hints: Look at the carbon skeletons of the two oxidation products, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and work out whether the starting $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH}$ must be primary or secondary.
walkthrough:
Use the products to identify the alcohol**
Both products contain the straight chain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}$. That is three carbons in a row with no branching. The aldehyde $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ and the carboxylic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ can only both form from a primary alcohol, so the starting alcohol must be $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, propan-1-ol.

Convert to skeletal**
In skeletal notation each bend and end of a line is a carbon, hydrogens on carbon are hidden, but the $\text{OH}$ group is shown in full. Draw a zig-zag of two lines (three carbons) like a sideways V, then write OH at one end: /\/OH.
Final answer: Skeletal formula of propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$: a three-carbon zig-zag chain with -OH on the end carbon.

hints: Decide what type of oxidation reaction 1 is by comparing propan-1-ol with propanoic acid in terms of full oxidation versus partial oxidation.
Recall the standard oxidising agent for alcohols and think about what laboratory set-up keeps a volatile aldehyde intermediate in the flask so it can be oxidised further.
walkthrough:
Recognise full oxidation**
Reaction 1 converts $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ all the way to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. That is primary alcohol to carboxylic acid, which goes via the aldehyde $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. You need a strong oxidant and vigorous conditions.

Choose reagent and condition**
The AS oxidant is acidified potassium dichromate(VI), written as $\text{H}^+ / \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$. To get the acid you must heat under reflux. Reflux condenses any aldehyde vapour and returns it to the flask, so it stays in contact with the oxidant long enough to be oxidised to the acid.
Final answer: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI), $\text{H}^+ / \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ ( $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ + dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ ); heat under reflux.

hints: Compare the product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ with the product of reaction 1 and decide whether this is partial or full oxidation.
Think about how the boiling points of aldehyde versus alcohol and acid allow you to remove one product from the oxidising mixture as soon as it forms.
walkthrough:
Recognise partial oxidation**
Reaction 2 stops at $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. That is primary alcohol to aldehyde only. You still use the same oxidant, $\text{H}^+ / \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$, but you must prevent further oxidation to propanoic acid.

Choose distillation to protect the aldehyde**
Propanal has a much lower boiling point than propan-1-ol and propanoic acid because it cannot hydrogen bond to itself. If you heat gently and distil, the aldehyde boils off as soon as it forms, leaves the flask, and is collected. Removed from the oxidant, it cannot be oxidised further.
Final answer: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI), $\text{H}^+ / \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ ( $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ + dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ ); heat and distil immediately.

hints: Identify reaction 3 as the reaction between the carboxylic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and the alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and recall the general family of the organic product.
walkthrough:
Spot esterification and name the ester**
Reaction 3 mixes an acid and an alcohol together: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. The organic product P is therefore an ester. Name it alkyl alkanoate: the alcohol part gives propyl, the acid part gives propanoate, so P is propyl propanoate.
